e.etymology: The Portuguese and Catalan form of Joachim, from Hebrew Yehoyaqim, the Lord will raise up. Tradition gives the name to the father of the Virgin Mary; the Spanish form is Joaquin.
From Arabic Maysa, one who walks with a graceful, swaying step. In Brazil Maysa is a separate name, a variant of Maisa, made famous by the singer Maysa.
A transliteration of Arabic Imad, pillar or support, often short for Imad al-Din, pillar of the faith. The Emad spelling follows Egyptian and Persian pronunciation.
A respelling of Niko or Nico, short forms of Nicholas, from Greek Nikolaos, victory of the people.
An Irish surname, from O Maoil Eoin, descendant of a devotee of Saint John. As a first name it rose in the late 2010s, when the rapper Post Malone became a star.

e.meaning: true bow, or truth and beauty, by the characters used
e.etymology: A Japanese girls' name written several ways, most simply as true bow or with characters for truth, reason and beauty. In Tagalog, mayumi is also a word for gentle and modest, which adds to its use in Filipino families.
A respelling of Zane with X for the Z sound. Zane is an American surname of uncertain origin that became a first name through Western novelist Zane Grey.
A respelling of Cataleya, the heroine's name in the 2011 film Colombiana, taken from the cattleya orchid, Colombia's national flower. The orchid was named for English botanist William Cattley.
An Indian name, common among Bengalis, usually explained as a form of Sanskrit abhika, fearless.
An Indian name from Sanskrit amaya, without guile or illusion, used as a name of the god Ganesha.
A recent American spelling in the family of Sariyah, Zariyah and Sariah. It is close to Seraiah, a Biblical man's name, but has no settled source of its own.
A short form of Lakshya, from Sanskrit lakshya, a target or aim, hence a goal in life.
The stage name of Puerto Rican trap singer Noriel, whose rise from 2016 to 2018 matches the name's US peak. It is also a given name in the Philippines. Its source is not settled.
The English word future, from Latin futurus, about to be, used as a modern word name. It is the stage name of Atlanta rapper Future, who also gave it to his son.
The English word for corn, from Spanish maiz, taken from Taino mahiz. As a name it sits with Maisie and Mae, and with the surnames Mays and Mayes.
A recent blend of Mia with -lani, the Hawaiian word for sky or heaven found in Leilani and Kailani.
A respelling of Ensley, an English surname related to Ainsley and Ansley, with a z in the manner of Kenzley and Kinzley.
A pet form of August, Augustus and Augustine, from Latin augustus, venerable or majestic. Auggie Pullman is the hero of the novel and film Wonder.
namesakes: Auggie Pullman (boy at the center of the novel and film Wonder)

assoc.t: Auggie Pullman, the boy of the novel and film Wonder

e.etymology: A respelling of Poppy, the red-flowered plant, from Old English popig. Poppy has long been popular in Britain and is rising in the US.
e.note: Poppi is the exact spelling of a widely sold prebiotic soda brand.

e.etymology: The English word purpose, an aim or reason for being, from Old French porpos. It is a recent American word name in the vein of Destiny, Journey and Legacy.
A spelling of Ainara, Basque for swallow, the bird, with an h as in Ainhoa, another Basque name. Both have spread from the Basque Country to Spain and Latin America.
A spelling of True that matches the German word treu, faithful or loyal, which is also a German surname. True itself is an English word name.

A spelling of Caitlin, the Irish form of Katherine, which came through Old French Cateline. In Irish it is said kat-LEEN, the source of Kathleen; English speakers have read the spelling as KAYT-lin since the 1970s.
namesakes: Kaitlin Olson (Dee on It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia)

e.etymology: An English surname, in part from the River Cary in Somerset and in part a form of Carey. Hollywood star Cary Grant, born Archibald Leach, made it a first name from the 1930s on.
namesakes: Cary Elwes (Westley in The Princess Bride)
e.note: Sounds the same as the girls' name Carrie.

assoc.t: Cary Grant, classic Hollywood leading man

e.etymology: A respelling of Valerie, the French form of the Roman family name Valeria, from Latin valere, to be strong or healthy.
A Spanish-language name common in Venezuela and elsewhere in Latin America. It is often described as indigenous Venezuelan in origin, though its source is not documented.
A pet form of Susan, Suzanne and Susannah, which go back to Hebrew Shoshannah, lily.
A respelling of Ryan, from the Irish surname Ó Riain, descendant of Rian. Rian is an old personal name traditionally linked to rí, king.
In the United States mostly a Spanish-language name, written Anaí, and a shorter form of Anahí, a name from a Guaraní legend about the ceibo flower.
The Spanish pet form of Adela, from the Germanic element adal, noble. La Adelita is a famous ballad of the Mexican Revolution, and the women who fought in it are called adelitas.
A blend of Emily or Emma with the -lyn ending. The same combination, from Emy and Lyn, is used in the Philippines.
A respelling of Gwendolyn, from Welsh Gwendolen: gwen, white, fair or blessed, with dolen, ring or loop.
